# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 72 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 72 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_072_page_001.jpg

---

## Council Notes

Chapter 72 continues the systematic rod interpretation, covering five more categories and reaching the highest — those whose rods are fully green with shoots and fruit, representing the martyrs.

The "double life" (*dipsychos* in practice) motif in 72:1 is rendered differently by the agents. EMET has "lived a double life," LOGOS "lived a divided life," PNEUMA "lived a double life." The Greek is not *dipsychos* here but a description of behavior — some good and some evil — so LOGOS's "divided life" captures the mixed moral state precisely.

The tower hierarchy (first, second, third) reflects a graduated eschatological scheme. First tower = best placement, second = good but delayed repentance, third = difficult entry. This system is consistent with the Visions section and is maintained throughout.

The phrase in 72:3, "envy and strife toward one another on account of matters of dignity and rank" (*peri prōteiōn kai peri doxēs tinos*), is a sharp critique of ecclesiastical status-seeking. All three agents render this consistently.

The climactic category in 72:5 — green rods with shoots and fruit — represents the martyrs: those who suffered for the name, endured with a whole heart, and "laid down their lives" (*apethēkan tas psychas autōn*). This is the highest category and the only one that needs no further explanation from the shepherd. All agents handle this reverently and correctly.

The main disagreements are in word choice for "divided/double life," "business dealings/affairs," and "fell away."

---

## Similitude 8, Part 3 — More Rod Categories

**72:1** "Those who surrendered their rods more dry than green — these are those who believed yet lived a divided life: they did some good but also committed much evil. Some of them repented and were placed in the first tower; others repented and were placed in the second tower; still others did not repent at all. These remain even now among the unrepentant."

**72:2** "Those who surrendered their rods more green than dry — these are those who for the most part led a good life but committed some evil, and who had not long been among the faithful. They repented quickly when they heard my commandments. Their dwelling is in the first tower."

**72:3** "Those who surrendered their rods green but with dried tips — these are those who were at all times good and faithful, yet who had some measure of envy and strife toward one another over matters of rank and dignity. When they heard my words, the greater part of them repented quickly, and their dwelling is in the first tower. Some were double-minded, and their dwelling is in the second tower."

**72:4** "Those who surrendered their rods half-green and half-dry — these are those who had become immersed in business dealings and had not kept close to the holy ones. For this reason half of them is living and half dead. Many of them, when they heard my commandments, repented; and those who repented dwell in the first tower. Some were altogether double-minded and fell away. These have lost their lives."

**72:5** "Those who surrendered their rods entirely green, with shoots and fruit — these are those who suffered hardship for the sake of the name and endured with a whole heart, and who laid down their lives."

---

*SOPHIA represents the consensus rendering of EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA, with rulings recorded in the Disagreement Log.*
